instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access the specified Coursera course page without signing in/enrolling (or record unavailability state)
criteria.description: Navigate to the Coursera course page using the provided URL (or the noted alternate starting URL context) and attempt to view the public course overview without signing in, enrolling, purchasing, or starting a trial. Full credit if the agent either (a) reaches the public course overview page, or (b) is blocked by an uncontrollable factor (login wall required to view details, CAPTCHA, region restriction, site error/404/removed) and clearly reports the availability/unavailability state encountered. Partial credit if the agent lands on a closely related Coursera page (e.g., variant course URL) but does not confirm it matches the requested course title. No credit if the agent signs in, enrolls, purchases, or starts a trial.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows a publicly viewable Coursera course overview page (logged out UI with Log In/Join for Free visible) for an IBM-branded course titled “Python for Data Science, AI & Development,” with an “Enroll for free” CTA. Action History indicates the agent was on https://www.coursera.org/learn/python-for-applied-data-science-ai and scrolled. Screenshot 2 also shows a logged-out Coursera overview section but not the title/URL.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Within constraints (no sign-in/enroll), the agent did access a live public Coursera course page. Although the page title shown is not exactly “Python for Applied Data Science,” the task explicitly notes the agent may have started on the -ai variant URL and should not be penalized for that context. No evidence of a login wall or constraint violation. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Coursera page in a logged-out state with a top navigation bar including the Coursera logo, “Explore”, “Degrees”, a search box (“What do you want to learn?”), and buttons “Log In” and “Join for Free”. The page content visible is a course overview section with headings like “What you’ll learn”, “Skills you’ll gain”, “Tools you’ll learn”, and “Details to know” (e.g., “Shareable certificate”, “Taught in English”, “Assessments 22 assignments”, and a “95% Most learners liked this course”). A right-side panel says “Your privacy and this chat” with a “Got it” button. The screenshot does NOT display the course title, instructor name, institution/partner name, or a syllabus section listing modules/weeks.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial success is supported by the screenshot: it appears the agent accessed a public Coursera course overview page without signing in (Log In/Join for Free visible; no account UI shown). However, the screenshot alone does not confirm it is the specified course (“Python for Applied Data Science”) or the alternate (“…-ai”) because the title/URL/instructor/institution are not visible in this capture. No evidence of enrollment/sign-in is present, which is good for the constraints.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims the page shows the course title (“Python for Data Science, AI & Development”), instructor (Joseph Santarcangelo), institution (IBM), and that the syllabus says “There are 5 modules…”. None of those elements are visible in the provided screenshot. Also, the predicted output mentions an “Enroll for free Starts Sep 9” button and “Included with Coursera Plus”, neither of which are visible in this screenshot (only “Join for Free” at the site header is visible).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Coursera course overview page (Coursera header with search bar and top tabs like “For Individuals”, “For Businesses”, etc.). Breadcrumb text near the top reads “Browse > Data Science > Data Analysis”. The page title area shows the IBM logo and the course title “Python for Data Science, AI & Development”. A blue button says “Enroll for free” with “Starts Sep 9” beneath it. No sign-in wall is shown; the top-right has “Log In” and “Join for Free”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms access to a public Coursera course overview page without signing in/enrolling (no login gate shown). However, it does not show the exact requested URL/title “Python for Applied Data Science”; instead it shows a related IBM course titled “Python for Data Science, AI & Development,” consistent with the alternate starting URL context mentioned in the prompt. This should be considered partial alignment with the specified course but still demonstrates successful access to a public course page without violating constraints.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output states the page corresponds to the requested course; the screenshot only shows the title “Python for Data Science, AI & Development” (not “Python for Applied Data Science”). The screenshot does not display the URL, so the agent’s claim about the exact URL on page is not verifiable from this image.

criteria.criterion: Record number of modules/weeks shown in the syllabus
criteria.description: Open, scroll to, or expand the syllabus section (as available on the public page) and report the number of modules/weeks listed. Full credit for the correct count as shown. Full credit if the syllabus is inaccessible or not fully loadable due to an uncontrollable blocker (login wall, region restriction, dynamic loading failure) and the agent states the count cannot be determined. Partial credit if the agent demonstrates an attempt to expand/view all weeks but can only provide an approximate/partial count due to collapsed sections or UI limitations.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the syllabus summary label “5 modules.” Screenshot 2 does not show module/week count.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The requested count (modules/weeks shown in syllabus) is supported: 5 modules. However, the agent additionally listed specific module titles that are not evidenced in the screenshots; that extra detail is not required for the criterion, but it is an unsupported claim. Minor penalty for over-claiming beyond evidence while still getting the core requested number correct.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the overview area below, a section header reads “5 modules” followed by text “Gain insight into a topic and learn the fundamentals.”

The agent’s predicted output stating “There are 5 modules in this course” is consistent with the visible “5 modules” text. The specific module titles listed by the agent are not visible in this screenshot, but the requested count is.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent listed the names of all 5 modules; the screenshot does not show any module list/titles—only the count “5 modules.”

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest DOM state 1 includes the course metadata showing “5 modules”. The DOM does not show an expanded syllabus listing module titles in the provided evidence; it only confirms the count.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The criterion primarily asks for the number of modules/weeks shown. The DOM explicitly supports “5 modules”, so full credit for the count. The agent’s additional list of module titles is not supported by DOM, but the criterion does not require titles—only the number—so no deduction is warranted here.

Full credit if an uncontrollable blocker prevents verification and the agent clearly states it cannot be confirmed. Partial credit if the agent reports uncertainty but accurately describes what was visible (e.g., only 'Enroll for Free' shown, no audit text).

criteria.criterion: Stop after recording overview and syllabus details (respect stopping condition and constraints)
criteria.description: Stop once instructor, institution, module/week count, and audit availability (or inability to verify due to blockers) have been recorded; do not proceed beyond overview/syllabus. Full credit if the agent stops appropriately and does not sign in, enroll, purchase, or start a trial. Partial credit if the agent performs minor extra navigation on the same public page but remains within constraints. No credit if the agent violates constraints or continues significantly beyond the requested scope.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows only a scroll action on the course page. Screenshots show only public overview content; no evidence of sign-in, enrollment, purchase, or trial initiation.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent stayed within constraints and (per output) stopped after recording overview/syllabus details. The single scroll is within scope. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows only overview-type sections (“What you’ll learn”, “Skills you’ll gain”, “Tools you’ll learn”, and “Details to know”) and does not show any checkout/enrollment flow, payment screen, or sign-in wall. The header shows logged-out options (“Log In”, “Join for Free”). There is no visible syllabus/module list to indicate deeper navigation beyond overview, and no visible action buttons like “Enroll” within this captured viewport.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Within what’s visible, the agent appears to remain on a public overview page and does not appear to have enrolled, purchased, started a trial, or signed in—consistent with constraints. However, the screenshot does not show that the agent actually recorded the required overview/syllabus details (instructor, institution, module/week count, audit availability) because those specific details are not visible here; thus we cannot confirm the stopping condition was met based on this screenshot. The agent’s single scroll action (per history) would be considered minor extra navigation, but the screenshot itself does not evidence the recorded syllabus details.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Predicted output states the agent recorded instructor, institution, a 5-module syllabus list, and assessed audit availability. The screenshot does not show the instructor/institution or any syllabus module/week breakdown, so the claim of having captured those from the visible page is not supported by this evidence. No contradiction regarding constraint violations is visible.
